text: More than 180 years ago, working men in Britain could not vote, because the vote went only to people who owned property.
Working men began to meet in groups, in London and in Carmarthen in Wales, to ask for change.
src: The Reform Act 1832 failed to extend the vote beyond those who owned property / launched 1838
William Lovett and Henry Hetherington founded the London Working Men’s Association / the Carmarthen Working Men’s Association began Chartism in Wales

text: In 1838 the Chartists set out their aims in the People's Charter, a list of six changes.
It asked for a vote for every man over twenty-one, a secret ballot, and pay for Members of Parliament.
src: The People’s Charter of 1838 asked for six reforms
a vote for every man over twenty-one, the secret ballot / payment of MPs

text: In 1839 more than a million people signed a petition, a long list of names, but Parliament refused to listen.
That year marchers went to a hotel in Newport, Wales, held by soldiers, and more than twenty Chartists were killed.
src: 1839: A petition signed by 1.3 million working people is presented to the House of Commons, which votes not to hear the petitioners
1839: John Frost leads several thousand marchers to the Westgate Hotel in Newport, where more than twenty Chartists are killed / which was held by soldiers

text: A second petition, with over three million names, was turned down too.
Strikes spread from the Staffordshire Potteries, and hundreds of strikers were put in prison.
src: A second petition of over three million signatures is rejected
a wave of strikes spreads from the Staffordshire Potteries / hundreds were imprisoned and dozens transported

text: Their best-loved leader was Feargus O'Connor, a tall man whose voice could reach huge crowds.
In 1847 he was elected for Nottingham, the only Chartist ever to become a Member of Parliament.
src: Feargus O’Connor, proprietor of the Northern Star, was its acknowledged leader and, in Thompson’s words, its “most well-loved man”: over six feet tall, with a voice that could carry to an open-air crowd of tens of thousands
1847: Feargus O’Connor is elected for Nottingham, the only Chartist ever to become an MP

text: Some Chartist leaders were sent to Australia as punishment, and miners there later asked for Chartist rights.
The movement faded, but later five of its six demands became law, among them the secret ballot.
src: Leaders transported to Australia spread their beliefs there / miners at the Eureka Stockade at Ballarat, Victoria, put forward Chartist demands
after it faded five of its six demands were enacted between 1867 and 1918 / the secret ballot came in 1872
